title: Treat-to-Target, Treat-to-Thrive: A Tool to Improve the Patient-Provider Partnership and Achieve Better Integrative Treatment Outcomes
session_type: Lifestyle and Behavioral Interventions - Sleep, nutrition, exercise, social support, alternative medicine | ARP
time_range: 10:00 AM - 11:30 AM East Coast USA Time
chairs_names: Grace Wright, MD, PhD, FACR (Interactive Moderator) | Erin Siceloff, PA-C (Session Coordinator)
chairs_geography: President & CEO, Grace C Wright MD PC | Arthritis and Osteoporosis Consultants of the Carolinas, Stallings, North Carolina
description:
Learning Objectives::
Attendees will describe their own patient-provider communication and engagement style and preferences. They will identify at least 3 key communication tools or strategies to support shared decision-making and follow-through in a treat-to-target approach in rheumatologyAttendees will demonstrate the ability to identify the Partnership Tool components: TREAT (T = Targets that matter; R = Relationships of support & trust; E = Examinations of symptoms/labs & changes; A = Alternative next steps; T = Team decisions), and THRIVE (T = Tools for pain/fatigue; H = Habits (exercise, sleep, nutrition); R = Relationships & social life; I = Inner world (mental health); V = Valued activities (connect to values); E = Executive functionsAttendees will increase their self-reported confidence in implementing a treat-to-target approach in their clinical setting as patient or provider, as well as their self-reported empathy for a variety of patient and provider experiences and contexts. Both of these measures will be recorded at the beginning and end of the sessionAttendees will assess at least one opportunity for future adaptation and implementation of the Partnership Tool, including methods for measuring patient engagement, communication quality, and clinical impact
